resources.version_label: Version of Record, Journal of Cold-Region Materials (2025)

paragraphs: We study lattice relaxation across five monitoring stations using a mixed-effects model.
Authors: Elif Varga, Elif Nakamura, Tamsin Kaczmarek. Published in Journal of Cold-Region Materials, 2025.
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station.

sections: Abstract

We report peak load measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2023 and 2025. A pilot survey in 2020 had put the regional peak load at 965.6 kN; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of lattice relaxation relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2022 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2025 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the peak load for each station in the 2025 campaign. The largest change relative to 2022 was observed at station M-09.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Jovanović et al. (2019). [2] Szabo and Mbeki (2021). [3] Pellegrini et al. (2022).
